message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported of abdominal aortic aneurysm (one is prevalent-only but still aligned). Several candidates report only full-model discrimination (or partial-r) or have missing PRS-comparable metrics, making cross-model ranking uncertain. PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA publication (“Genetic Architecture of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm in the Million Veteran Program.”) and provides a clear PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and a reasonable validation size (n=46,564). Competing framework-style scores (PGS001784 from a global biobank framework; PGS002054 from a UKB portability framework) either emphasize broader pan-trait development context or provide only weak PRS-comparable metrics (e.g., partial-r ~0.0144; R2 ~0.0147) alongside full-model AUROC values that are not directly comparable as PRS-only evidence; UKB-based models (PGS003429) and the Nat Genet PRS-CS models (PGS003972/PGS003973) report full-model AUROC/C-index without PRS-only metrics and have unknown/variable covariate transparency, limiting interpretability. Because key performance fields are missing or not comparable across most candidates (PRS-only AUROC largely absent; covariates unknown in some; outlier full-model metrics likely covariate-driven), the selection remains only moderately supported."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA). Several candidates report only full-model discrimination (e.g., AUROC/C-index) with missing or unclear PRS-only/incremental metrics and/or unknown covariates (PGS003429/PGS003972/PGS003973), making cross-model performance comparison unreliable. Two candidates are clearly framework/portability-style (PGS001784: Global Biobank analyses; PGS002054: UKB portability) and should not automatically outrank a disease-focused AAA study absent clearly superior PRS-only evidence. PGS000753 comes from an AAA-focused Circulation study, uses basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and provides a supportive per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with moderate validation size (n=46,564); however, it lacks explicit AUC/R2, so the choice remains uncertain versus newer multi-cohort PRS-CS scores (PGS003972/PGS003973) that report high full-model discrimination but with limited transparency on PRS-only contribution. Therefore a direct match exists but the best-supported selection is only weakly determined from the visible evidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have diagnosis-like phenotyping_reported (“abdominal aortic aneurysm” or “prevalent abdominal aortic aneurysm”). However, PRS-comparable performance evidence is sparse/inconsistent across the set: only PGS001784 reports a covariates-regressed-out PRS R2 (0.014661), while several others report only full-model AUROC/C-index (e.g., PGS003973 C-index 0.882; PGS003429 AUROC 0.708; PGS003972 AUROC 0.69) with missing incremental/PRS-only AUROC, and covariates are unknown for two of the disease-focused 2023 models (PGS003429/PGS003972). PGS001784 comes from a global biobank framework paper (pan-trait style), which domain guidance says should be penalized when disease-focused alternatives exist unless it has clearly stronger endpoint+metric evidence; here its advantage is mainly metric availability. PGS000753 is a disease-focused AAA publication (Circulation; AAA-specific genetic architecture), uses only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and provides an effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) supporting PRS signal, but it lacks AUC/R2 and uses a prevalent endpoint, limiting direct comparability. Given these limitations and competing but non-comparable full-model metrics, selection is not strongly supported, so confidence remains low."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are abdominal aortic aneurysm, with one explicitly “prevalent”). Several candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index (e.g., PGS001784 AUROC=0.868 with extensive age interaction terms; PGS003973 C-index=0.882) or have unknown covariates (PGS003429/PGS003972), making PRS-only comparability unclear per the provided domain rules (do not substitute full-model AUROC as PRS performance). PGS000753 is selected because it comes from a disease-focused AAA publication (MVP/Mayo; Circulation), has a clean, clinically interpretable endpoint (“Prevalent abdominal aortic aneurysm”) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), and provides a PRS effect size (OR per SD=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) as supportive evidence of discrimination without relying on potentially covariate-driven full-model AUC. Main limitation: lack of PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 across most models and heterogeneous/unclear metric definitions prevents a high-confidence, clearly best choice among the direct-match set."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm, though one is explicitly prevalent). Several candidates report only full-model discrimination (e.g., AUROC/C-index) that is not PRS-comparable and/or have unknown covariates (PGS003429, PGS003972), while two come from pan-trait/portability framework contexts (PGS001784: Global Biobank analyses; PGS002054: Portability of 245 polygenic scores), which domain guidance down-ranks when disease-focused alternatives exist. PGS000753 is from a disease-focused AAA publication (MVP/Mayo-VDB), has basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), and provides an interpretable per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with moderate validation size (n=46,564). However, confidence remains low because it lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 and there is meaningful unresolved competition from newer disease-focused PRS-CS models (PGS003972/PGS003973) whose very high reported full-model metrics cannot be cleanly interpreted without clearer PRS-only/incremental metrics and comparable covariate reporting."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (all abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA). However, comparable PRS-only performance evidence is sparse or non-comparable across models: several report only full-model AUROC/C-index (e.g., PGS001784 AUROC=0.868 with extensive covariates; PGS003973 C-index=0.882 with age/sex; PGS003429 AUROC=0.708; PGS003972 AUROC=0.69), while others report weak PRS-comparable metrics (PGS001784 Nagelkerke R2 covariates regressed out=0.014661; PGS002054 partial-r=0.0144). Per domain guidance, full-model AUROC should not be substituted for PRS-only discrimination, and covariate-heavy models risk being mostly covariate-driven; thus the very high AUROC/C-index values are not decisive. Given this, PGS000753 is selected because it is from a disease-focused AAA paper and provides a PRS effect size (OR per SD=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates, offering direct evidence of PRS contribution without relying on potentially covariate-inflated full-model AUROC. Confidence remains low because other strong disease-focused multi-cohort candidates (PGS003972/PGS003973) lack PRS-only metrics and appear competitive, and the available metadata do not allow a clean, apples-to-apples performance comparison across the set."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm), so a direct match exists. Among them, PGS003972 (PRS-CS; Nat Genet 2023 AAA GWAS meta-analysis) is best supported by study context: it comes from a disease-focused multi-cohort meta-analysis with broad development cohorts (many AAA-relevant studies/biobanks), aligning with the domain guidance to prefer disease-focused multi-cohort models over framework/portability scores when endpoints are similarly aligned. Competing options have notable limitations: PGS001784 (Global Biobank/Cell Genomics) and PGS002054 (UKB portability paper) are explicitly framework/portability-derived; PGS000753 is an older, very sparse P+T (29 variants) with only an OR reported; and PGS003429 is a screening/cost-effectiveness paper with unknown covariates and only full-model metrics. Between the two Nat Genet sister scores (PGS003972 vs PGS003973), the visible evidence is insufficient to clearly favor one: PGS003973 reports a high full-model C-index (0.882) but with basic covariates only (age, age^2, sex) and small validation size, while PGS003972 reports a lower full-model AUROC (0.69) with unknown covariates; neither provides PGS-only AUROC/R2 to isolate PRS contribution. Because the decisive PRS-comparable metrics and covariate comparability are missing/ambiguous—especially for the seemingly high C-index—confidence is low and the overall outcome is direct-match but sub-optimal rather than high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported (all are abdominal aortic aneurysm endpoints; one is explicitly prevalent AAA). However, the evidence is not sufficient to identify a single clearly best-supported model because reported performance is not comparable across candidates: several provide only full-model AUROC/C-index (often with unknown covariates), one provides only partial-r, and only one reports a PRS-only (covariates-regressed-out) R2. The two PRS-CS models from the 2023 Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis (PGS003972/PGS003973) look disease-focused and endpoint-faithful, but their headline discrimination metrics are full-model and not directly PRS-comparable; one reports a very high C-index (0.882) with only age/sex covariates but without PGS-only or incremental metrics, leaving uncertainty about PRS contribution. The large global-biobank framework score (PGS001784) reports a small covariates-regressed-out R2 (0.014661) consistent with the heritability sanity-check, but it is a pan-framework context and its reported AUROC (0.868) is full-model with many covariates, limiting comparability. Given these conflicts, PGS000753 is selected as a reasonable direct-match option because it comes from a disease-focused AAA paper (Circulation; MVP/Mayo-VDB), reports a meaningful per-SD effect size (OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates, and has moderate validation size (n=46,564), but missing AUC/R2 prevents a high-confidence choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All six candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are abdominal aortic aneurysm, with one explicitly “prevalent” AAA). Ranking by the provided policy favors disease-focused, endpoint-faithful models over pan-trait/portability frameworks when performance evidence is not clearly and comparably stronger. PGS000753 comes from an AAA-focused Circulation paper (“Genetic Architecture of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm in the Million Veteran Program”), has a direct prevalent AAA endpoint, basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), and provides a PRS-relevant effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) in a reasonably sized validation (n=46,564). Competing models with explicit AUROC/R2 are either from framework-style papers (PGS001784: Global Biobank analyses; PGS002054: UKB portability) or report only full-model discrimination with unknown covariates (PGS003429, PGS003972) making cross-model PRS-only comparability unclear; PGS003973 reports a high C-index (0.882) but without clarity on whether this is PRS-driven versus baseline covariate-driven, so it cannot be cleanly used to outrank the disease-focused evidence package. Confidence is not high because multiple candidates lack PRS-only metrics and covariate details, and one candidate shows much higher full-model discrimination (PGS003973) that could be meaningful but is not interpretable from the visible metadata alone."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and all report an abdominal aortic aneurysm diagnosis endpoint (PGS000753 specifies prevalent AAA; others use generic AAA). Among the disease-focused candidates, PGS003972 and PGS003973 come from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet 2023; many contributing cohorts) with genome-wide PRS-CS construction, which domain_knowledge favors over portability/pan-trait framework scores when endpoint fidelity is comparable. PGS003972 is preferred because it has multiple validation records (record_count=3) and a more conservative, interpretable full-model AUROC (0.69) rather than the very high C-index reported for PGS003973 (0.882), which could be heavily covariate-driven and is not directly comparable to PRS-only performance (and no PGS-only AUROC/R2 is provided). Main limitation: across the direct-match set, truly PRS-comparable metrics are sparse (most report only full-model AUROC/C-index or partial-r), covariates are unknown for several models (including PGS003972), and the heritability sanity-check cannot be applied cleanly without PGS-only metrics; therefore confidence cannot be high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches at the EFO/trait level for age-related macular degeneration, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and strength/comparability of reported performance. PGS004606 is preferred because it has a clean, direct disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported: “Age-related macular degeneration”), is disease-focused (Nat Genet AMD genetics paper; IAMDGC development cohort), has large European validation (n=163,011), and reports discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.71) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs 1–10), making it more interpretable than portability-framework scores. Competing models are weaker on key dimensions: PGS001834/PGS002041 come from a UKB portability framework and only report small partial correlations (~0.016–0.018) rather than directly comparable PRS AUROC/R2; PGS002269 has phenotype ambiguity (phenotyping_reported retinal layer thickness despite AMD label) and lacks AUC/R2; PGS004607 shows lower AUROC (0.65) and GWAS ancestry mismatch (AFR GWAS evaluated in EUR); PGS004952 reports a very high AUROC but the metric appears inconsistently represented (classification_metrics AUROC ‘84.2’ vs full_model_auc 0.842) and is based on a small validation sample (n=1,232) and a narrower endpoint (“Late” AMD), reducing robustness for generic AMD. Remaining limitation: across candidates, PRS-only (no-covariate) AUROC/R2 and incremental metrics are largely missing, so selection relies on full-model AUROC/effect-size/context rather than fully comparable PRS-only performance, lowering confidence from High to Moderate."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_efo (age-related macular degeneration), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and comparability of performance evidence. PGS004606 has the cleanest endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Age-related macular degeneration), comes from a disease-focused AMD study (Nat Genet; IAMDGC development cohort listed), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) and has a large European validation sample (n=163,011) with a reported AUROC=0.71 using only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs 1-10), making it the most broadly supported package among the visible options. Competing models are weaker on key dimensions: PGS004607 is also disease-endpoint but shows lower AUROC (0.65) in the same validation ancestry; PGS001834 and PGS002041 are from a portability/framework paper with only small partial correlations (~0.016–0.018) and a less specific phenotype string; PGS002269 has phenotype mismatch (retinal layer thickness) despite AMD labeling; and PGS004952 reports a very high AUROC but is for late AMD and has a small validation size (n=1,232) plus an apparent metadata inconsistency (AUROC estimate shown as 84.2), reducing trust/comparability. Confidence is moderate (not high) because the selected AUROC is a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only) and several candidates have missing or non-comparable performance fields, limiting decisive cross-model performance comparison."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches via trait_efo=age-related macular degeneration, but endpoint fidelity differs: PGS004606/PGS004607 use phenotyping_reported='Age-related macular degeneration' (best-aligned), whereas PGS001834/PGS002041 use a vaguer 'Macular degeneration (senile) of retina NOS', PGS004952 targets 'Late age-related macular degeneration', and PGS002269 has a phenotype string focused on retinal layer thickness (proxy/adjacent endpoint despite AMD label). Among the best-aligned endpoint models, PGS004606 has higher reported full-model AUROC (0.71 vs 0.65 for PGS004607) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and a much larger validation sample (n=163,011), making it the best-supported choice from the visible evidence. Limitation: no PGS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental metrics are provided for these models, so the reported AUROC cannot be cleanly attributed to PRS contribution; this missing comparability evidence prevents a high-confidence, high-quality direct-match recommendation."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo=age-related macular degeneration), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and the comparability/availability of PRS-specific performance metrics. PGS004606 is best supported overall because it has an explicitly aligned disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Age-related macular degeneration), is disease-focused (IAMDGC development cohort; Nat Genet AMD architecture paper rather than a pan-trait portability framework), and provides interpretable discrimination evidence with only basic covariates (full-model AUROC=0.71; OR per SD=1.76) in a large European validation (n=163,011). Key limitations: the reported AUROC appears to be full-model rather than PGS-only, incremental/PGS-only metrics are not shown, and another candidate (PGS004952) reports a much higher AUROC but on a narrower endpoint (late AMD) with a very small validation sample (n=1,232) and potential metric reporting inconsistency (AUROC shown as 84.2). The UKB portability models (PGS001834/PGS002041) have PRS-comparable partial-r but are from a framework portability study with modest effect size (partial-r ~0.016–0.018) and less disease-specific endpoint evidence, so they do not clearly outrank PGS004606."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All six candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo is age-related macular degeneration; trait_reported is AMD or near-synonymous). Prioritizing endpoint fidelity, PGS004606 has a direct disease endpoint in phenotyping_reported (“Age-related macular degeneration”), comes from a disease-focused AMD GWAS consortium context (IAMDGC; Nat Genet), and reports discrimination (classification_metrics AUROC=0.71) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), plus a relatively large validation sample (n=163,011). Competing models include: (i) PGS004607 (same paper/method but weaker AUROC=0.65 and OR=1.48 vs OR=1.76), (ii) PGS001834/PGS002041 from a UKB portability framework with only small partial correlations (~0.016–0.018) and no AUC/R2, (iii) PGS002269 with phenotype mismatch/ambiguity (phenotyping_reported is retinal layer thickness rather than AMD diagnosis), and (iv) PGS004952 targeting late AMD specifically with a very small validation sample (n=1,232) and an AUROC field that appears internally inconsistent in the metadata (84.2 vs 0.842), making its apparent performance advantage hard to trust from this context alone. Overall, PGS004606 is best supported, but confidence is limited because key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUC/R2, incremental AUC) are not reported for most candidates and reported AUCs are full-model rather than explicitly PRS-only."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (alcohol dependence/alcohol use disorder), but the visible evidence is limited by missing standard comparable metrics (AUC/R2 are null across models) and some missing covariate reporting. PGS002738 has the strongest endpoint alignment (trait_efo: alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported: Alcohol use disorder) and provides the clearest discrimination-style evidence via an OR(top 10% vs rest)=1.96 (95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a sizable European evaluation sample (n=7,900), with development in disease-focused cohorts (MVP, UKB). Competing options PGS000201/PGS000202 use a closely related ‘problematic alcohol use’ label and report only small ΔR² (0.01192 and 0.00456) plus betas; PGS000202 also has a much smaller validation size (n=1,251). PGS002739 is African American evaluation-specific (AFR 100%) and thus less universally deployable without a specified target ancestry, and while it reports OR=1.76, it is not a closer direct match than PGS002738 for generic selection. Remaining limitation: lack of PRS-only AUC/R2 and unknown covariates for PGS002738 prevent a high-confidence ‘best’ determination despite its stronger effect-size evidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct matches in the sense that they target alcohol dependence/AUD-related endpoints: PGS002738 and PGS002739 explicitly report “Alcohol use disorder” with trait_efo=alcohol dependence, while PGS000201/PGS000202 report “Problematic alcohol use” but their phenotyping_reported is AUD DSM-5 criteria count (log-transformed), which is closely aligned to alcohol dependence. Among these, PGS002738 is best supported by endpoint fidelity (AUD case definition), multi-cohort disease-focused development context (MVP + UKB), and a directly interpretable discrimination-type metric (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a reasonably sized European evaluation (n=7,900). Main limitation: across candidates, standard PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2) are largely missing and covariates are unknown for PGS002738 (and PGS002739), which prevents a high-confidence selection and forces reliance on heterogeneous effect-size/ΔR2 reporting."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (alcohol dependence/alcohol use disorder), but they differ in endpoint labeling and strength/clarity of reported performance. PGS002738 has the most target-faithful labeling (trait_efo: alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported: Alcohol use disorder) and provides a clear discriminative effect size in validation (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) with a reasonably large European evaluation sample (n=7,900), supporting meaningful stratification.
